text:
mira: Heads-up — between 14:12-14:20 we saw a KV-cache miss storm in eu-west rack18 affecting fractional/dedicated slices. p99s spiked and some hosted tenants saw tail latency blips. Suspect NVMe/PCIe IO saturation from a few large embedding batch jobs. Anyone on-call?

tess: I pulled the rack telemetry. There's a correlated NVMe write latency spike and PCIe AER warnings on node 18-4. Dmesg shows repeated 'nvme0: timeout' entries. cc @sam

sam: Which job ids are hammering it? Can we soft-throttle them instead of draining the whole shelf?

mira: job ids 9876, 9880 — embeddings_app-runner. They switched to tokenizer batch_size=8192 yesterday. infra-bot posted metrics to #alerts.

infra-bot: Alert: KV_CACHE_MISS_RATE > 25% in eu-west-1a at 14:12 UTC; NVME_WRITE_LATENCY > 50ms; async ops backlog rising.

jonah: If NVMe is saturated we get KVCACHE eviction -> cascading cold starts. Short-term: limit concurrency for those jobs or move them to preemptible pool with NVMe priority. Long-term: we need IO headroom guards on dedicated slices.

tess: I can start a targeted drain of new jobs off rack18 to warmpool but that'll cause more migrations which might worsen IO. Running the drain playbook is /runbooks/drain-shelf.sh (dry-run first).

sam: Don't do a full drain yet. Try reducing concurrency to 2 for embeddings_app and enable prefix-kvcache on model:v2. That should reduce write amplification without heavy migrations.

mira: Applying concurrency=2 for tenant embeddings_app now (policy update). Monitoring tokens/sec and KV miss rate.

infra-bot: Action taken: quota update for tenant embeddings_app -> concurrency=2 at 14:18 UTC.

jonah: Early numbers: KV miss rate down from 27% -> 8% within 4 minutes; p99 gen latency dropped from ~320ms -> ~110ms. Looks stable so far.

tess: :thumbsup: I'll follow up with an RFC for routing policy to prefer NVMe-priority racks for heavy-IO embeddings and add an IO headroom budget for dedicated slices. Filing RFC now.

sam: Agreed. Also flag this for billing/product: dedicated customers running huge batch-tokenizers should be offered guidance (or a 'high-io' addon). @mira can you add an incident note and link to the runbook?

mira: Done — incident logged: https://redwood.ops/incident/INC-2026-045. Added remediation steps and temp quota change to the incident body.

jonah: Next steps: (1) Keep concurrency=2 for 30m then reassess; (2) draft routing IO-guard RFC; (3) add metric alert for NVMe AER events + KV miss high.

tess: I'll start the RFC draft and ping infra-design.

mira: Thanks all — keeping an eye. If anything regresses I'll call for a manual drain.
